editorial.marketOverview: Saturday's US cash market is closed, so Friday's steep AI-led selloff remains the last confirmed trading session. Reuters reports Nasdaq Composite down 5.28%, with semiconductor losses around 11%; a secondary close report places QQQ down 5.67%. Barron's reports Friday VIX closing at 37.66. The relative weakness of chips versus the broader Nasdaq supports elevated downside risk, while extreme volatility also raises the odds of a sharp countertrend bounce. These are Friday observations, not Saturday quotes.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the prior 07:32 EST snapshot, fresh review of Reuters' November 20 global selloff report and November 21 AP/FT coverage adds context but no new trading observation or material catalyst. Curated Open Watch is unchanged at 174 events and 2026-11-21T00:44:37+00:00. Bias, confidence, event risk and the three-session horizon are unchanged.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The confirmed market response was a broad Friday decline with disproportionate semiconductor damage and elevated protection demand. Expected effects of future PMI, confidence, earnings or inflation releases remain scenarios, not observations. Older 10Y 4.94% and 2Y 4.65% yield observations imply +29 basis points mathematically but are stale; the later 10Y quote cannot be mixed into a synchronized curve. Direct VXN, FedWatch and contract-aligned oil quotes are not verified. Reports differ on whether Nasdaq 100 definitively crossed the 20% bear threshold at the close, so that label is not relied upon for directional change.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: potential gap volatility and relief rally attempts after Friday's rout; flash PMIs can test growth and rate narratives. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Analog Devices/Dell results can test demand and semiconductor confidence. Wednesday November 25: PCE, GDP and other macro releases plus the Fed Beige Book could reprice rates and risk appetite. Bearish continuation remains the baseline, but any bounce needs broad semiconductor participation and falling volatility before changing the path.
editorial.bullCase: Oversold positioning and VIX above 37 may support forceful short-covering. A credible reversal would show QQQ and SOX/SMH recovering together, improving advance-decline participation and declining VIX/VXN, ideally alongside a verified decline in rate pressure.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's disproportionate chip losses and poor breadth imply forced selling may persist into Monday, especially if rebounds fail and volatility stays elevated. Disappointing PMI, AI hardware guidance or inflation releases would be additional bearish catalysts only if actually reported and market-confirmed.
editorial.watchNext: At Monday open verify synchronized QQQ/Nasdaq/SOX/SMH, breadth, VIX/VXN, paired 2Y/10Y yields, CME FedWatch and contract-matched Brent/WTI.
